title: Inverted arrows act by weak equivalences on hammock mapping spaces
statement:
Let $C$ be a small category, let $W$ be a wide subcategory, and use the reduced-hammock simplicial category $H(C,W)$ of [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation]. For any $u:x\to y$ in $W$ and $v\in C$, concatenation with the one-arrow hammock $u$ induces weak homotopy equivalences
$$H(C,W)(v,x)\longrightarrow H(C,W)(v,y),\qquad H(C,W)(y,v)\longrightarrow H(C,W)(x,v).$$
A weak homotopy equivalence means a map whose geometric realization is bijective on components and induces isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups. No freeness or calculus-of-fractions assumption is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 3.3, printed p.21. No Stacks tag states this result.
